Aluminum Association of Canada (1999). Options Paper for the Aluminum Industry. Report of the Minerals and Metals Working Group of the Industry Issues Table to the National Climate Change Secretariat, October 1999 (Canadian National Climate Change Process). Prepared for the working group by the Aluminum Association of Canada (stated in Sect. 2; the title page names only the working group).

Region: Canada (11 smelters, 2.3 Mt/yr capacity). Locators are PRINTED page numbers. Loaded: CF4 emission factors by smelter technology (HSS, VSS, SWPB, CWPB 180 kA and 300 kA) for 1996 and 2000+, with derived C2F6 (10% of CF4) and PFC CO2e; capex per t of installed capacity for replacing HSS with CWPB. Measures file: computer control and point-breaker-feeder retrofits, HSS replacement, allowance cost. NOT in this paper (despite the request): any specific energy consumption in kWh/t (the paper gives only sector energy totals and fuel shares; the 59 GJ/t and 13 kWh/kg figures are in the Foundation Paper nccp_1999_003) and any cost per tonne of CO2e. TRAPS: (1) The CF4 factors here differ from the Foundation Paper (nccp_1999_003, Table 5-5: HSS 0.3, VSS 0.9-1.0, SWPB 0.4, CWPB-180 0.15) and from the Hatch report (nccp_1999_004 Table 6-5, which implies 1990 factors); this paper says its figures supersede the Environment Canada factors and are interim. (2) Table 3 prints the NRCan factor as CF6. (3) Dollar amounts are printed with CA$ or $ and no price year; publication year 1999 used. (4) The CA$200 million point-feeder cost is for a typical 250,000 t smelter (a VSS retrofit); the foundation paper quotes CA$100-500 million per smelter. (5) Table 1 capacity totals and the BAU production (2,270 kt in 1996) differ slightly.
